request.instructions:
You audit the close of a design session for 3D printing in OpenSCAD. The harness verified the final version of the design and gives you, in JSON, what it measured (VERIFIED) and the spec adjustments it detected: changes of the spec towards what the mesh already measured, without the part changing (ADJUSTMENTS). Read the designer's CLOSE and answer only with a JSON object, with no text before or after it:
{"unsupported": [{"claim": "...", "reason": "..."}], "untold_adjustments": [{"adjustment": "...", "reason": "..."}]}
- unsupported: every claim the close presents as verified (measured, checked, that it meets, that it fits, that it does not collide, that it goes in, that it prints without supports) that VERIFIED does not back: it is not there, it says something else or the numbers do not match. Leave out: what the close states as not verified, an opinion, an intention, or a description of the design that does not claim to have been checked.
- untold_adjustments: every part of ADJUSTMENTS whose adjustments the close does not mention with their reason (one mention per part saying what was adjusted and why is enough).
Empty lists if there is nothing to object to. Be precise: quote the claim as it is written.

CLOSE
The desk jar is done: a two-part bayonet design in `model.scad` (part selector: `jar`, `lid`, `assembly`).

**The design**
- **Jar** — 70 mm bore × 80 mm deep (floor top to rim), 2.4 mm walls/floor, printed upright. A reduced neck (Ø61 opening, 3.7 mm wall) carries three L-shaped bayonet slots: open entry grooves at the rim plus horizontal locking grooves with 45° ceilings so nothing needs supports. A funnel cone inside eases pouring things back out.
- **Lid** — printed top-down, Ø74.8 mm exactly matching the jar body so it sits flush when closed. Three inward lugs (1.6 mm engagement, 0.4 mm clearance on every sliding face) drop into the entries and ride the slots through a 90° quarter-turn. At the locked end each groove floor has a 0.45 mm detent pocket: the lid rides raised on its lugs during the turn, then drops in with a click — to open you lift slightly and turn back. 24 shallow grip flutes and 45° edge chamfers all round keep it soft-edged and support-free.

**Verified**
- Both parts compile clean and are single watertight bodies with 0 bad edges [[jar]] [[lid]]; the closed jar is 74.8 × 74.8 × 86.0 mm [[assembly]].
- Interior measures Ø70 × 80 mm deep [[cavity]] with the Ø61 neck opening clear [[neck_opening]] [[slot_entry]]; walls 2.4 mm [[body_wall]], floor 2.4 mm [[floor]], neck wall 3.7 mm [[neck_wall]], lid skirt 2.8 mm [[skirt_wall]], cap 2.4 mm [[cap]] — all above the 1.6 mm minimum.
- Lugs present and sized as designed [[lug]], detent pockets empty and in place [[detent_pocket]]; groove [[decorative_groove]] and flutes [[grip_flutes]] inspected up close in the final meshes.
- Printability: jar has 0 mm² of overhang beyond 45° except 4.1 mm² of declared pocket ceilings, lid only its declared 45° lug faces; both fit the A1 bed with ≥90 mm margin [[G5]]. Bed contact 3936 mm² each [[base]] [[lid/top_on_bed]] [[assembly]].
- The quarter-turn motion sweeps −90°…0° with no collision, and the drop-on-and-turn assembly order passes [[lid_lock_turn]] [[assembly_order]].

**Not verified**
- Physical feel: detent click strength, turning torque and long-term PETG wear depend on your printer's calibration — the 0.4 mm clearances are nominal; if your PETG prints tight, scale the lid 100.5 % or sand a lug.
- Strength under drops/loads and the exact look of the fluted lid weren't tested.
- Spec adjustments to flag: the neck-opening check box was shrunk to fit inside the Ø61 bore it measures (my first box's corners poked into the neck wall — the geometry never changed, the box was badly posed). The neck-wall thickness ray was re-aimed to a lug-free azimuth for the same reason. The original protruding detent bump was genuinely redesigned into the drop-in pocket: a rigid quarter-turn sweep cannot pass an interference bump, and the pocket gives the same "won't open on its own" hold with zero swept overlap.
